HushPinterest 0.0.7 has 27 patches for Pinterest 14.39.0. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. A patched Pinterest can now sign up for push notifications, which Google's Firebase used to refuse, and you can pick the folder your downloads go to. Hide ads also looks inside the rows of pins on Home and under a pin, and Hide shopping catches store product pins.

This release moves to Pinterest 14.39.0. Patch 14.39.0 and install it over your current HushPinterest with the same signing key, and your settings stay as they are.

## What's new

- Pinterest 14.39.0 is now the supported version. All 27 patches apply to it, and 14.38.0 is no longer a target.
- New Fix push notifications patch, on by default. Google's Firebase service only signs Pinterest up for push notifications when the request names Pinterest's original signature, and a patched Pinterest is signed with a different one, so it never got a notification token. The patch gives Firebase the original signature's fingerprint when Pinterest signs up and changes nothing else in the request. Its switch is on the new Notifications page under More settings.
- Download pins has a new Save in Pinterest's folder switch, and it starts off. With it on, downloads go to Pictures/100PINT/Pins, the folder Pinterest's own image saves use, instead of filling up Download. Board downloads, long-press downloads and retries from Download history follow it too, and the download messages and Download history point to that folder instead of Downloads. (#5)
- Download pins can also save into a folder you pick. Tap Pick a download folder and choose any folder inside Pictures, DCIM, Download or Documents in Android's folder picker. Android's Downloads still does the saving, so nothing gets copied and no storage permission is needed. Each download in Download history remembers its folder, so its messages point there even after you pick another. Tap the row again to pick a different folder or go back to Download. Save in Pinterest's folder wins while it's on, and picking a folder turns it off. (#5)
- Long-press download keeps Pinterest's own buttons again. Holding a pin in a grid showed only Download, because Pinterest's Pin, Share and More ideas buttons never sprang back in after the patch laid the menu out again. Now all three show with Download after them, and letting go on any of them does what it says.
- System share sheet opens Android's share menu from a pin's Share button on 14.39.0. The pin's id is now read from the fields Pinterest's share sheet fills, found when you patch, instead of by a name that pointed somewhere else in 14.39.0, which left Pinterest's own sheet showing with the switch on.
- Hide advertising ID now keeps Pinterest's browser ID out of Google's Block Store too. Pinterest kept it there so that, on a phone with Google backup on, it would outlast an uninstall and come back on a new phone, which let a fresh install send the old ID before you'd signed in. With the switch on, Pinterest finds no saved ID, and when it tries to save one it deletes the stored copy instead, so a reinstall starts fresh. The browser cookie for the install you're using keeps working the way it did.
- The settings home ends with a Support HushPinterest row. Tapping it opens the Ko-fi page in your browser, and if no app can open it you get a message with the address instead. Its text is translated into German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish.
- Download board no longer saves a board's pins a second time once they've dropped off Download history. The history still shows the newest 32 entries, and it now remembers the 500 before those. Removing a pin from Download history forgets its older downloads too.
- Morphe Manager and the patch index now show the HushPinterest icon next to the source instead of the owner's GitHub picture.
- Hide ads now looks inside modules. A row of ideas on Home or a group of pins under the pin you opened carries its own pins, and an ad in one got through because Hide ads only checked the row itself. Now the ad comes out of the row, and a row left with nothing in it goes too, heading and all. Hide AI-labeled pins and Hide shopping reach inside rows the same way. A pin that carries Pinterest's promotion or campaign ID also counts as an ad now. (#6)
- Hide shopping and product pins now hides a shop's product pins, the ones shown with a store name like Target or Nordstrom Rack and a tag icon under the picture. Pinterest doesn't mark them as paid, so Hide ads keeps leaving them alone, but they slipped past Hide shopping too. With Debug logging on, the diagnostic report also lists the shopping and ad fields of what stays, so a pin that still gets through can be tracked down. (#6)
- Hide ads now catches shopping spotlight stories on the feed models that keep the story kind as Pinterest's own type rather than as text. Before, only the text form counted, so a spotlight on those models stayed unless Hide shopping was on too. Other stories stay put, and Hide shopping still works on its own.
- If a Pinterest update leaves Hide ads only part of its hooks, the Feed page now names the feed lists and ad panels it couldn't reach instead of reading as if everything's covered. The diagnostic report lists every list and panel with how much of it went in, and names the two places no hook reaches yet (Shopping ideas groups in search results and shopping wrappers under related pins). A full build reads the same as before.
- Strip link tracking has a new Plain pin links switch on the Privacy page, and it starts off. With it on, a pin.it link you copy or share becomes the pin's own pinterest.com link, so it doesn't tell Pinterest who shared it. Links Pinterest makes for Copy link or a share change right away, even when you send a pin straight to another app, because HushPinterest sees which pin Pinterest made the link for. Any other short link you copy is checked with Pinterest in the background and swapped on the clipboard a moment later, as long as you haven't copied something else by then. Shared text never waits for that check, and if it fails or takes longer than 4 seconds the short link stays. A pin link from one of Pinterest's country sites, like de.pinterest.com or www.pinterest.co.uk, becomes the same www.pinterest.com link with no lookup, and a pin's sent link drops the invite code that ties it to whoever sent it. Board links and account pages stay as they are, and so does a pin link that still carries a parameter after tracking tags come off.
- HushPinterest settings has a new page under More settings, Pinterest's own settings. It shows where Pinterest keeps its own theme, privacy, notification, AI content and cellular autoplay settings, and names each step through Pinterest's menus in the language Pinterest is using. HushPinterest doesn't change any of them. The AI content row explains how it differs from Hide AI-labeled pins, and the autoplay row says Pinterest may still load part of a video ahead of time.
- HushPinterest drops its Android 9 code now that Pinterest 14.39.0 needs Android 10. The file picker saves go, along with their Pending saves page, and so does the app folder Android 9 used for diagnostic reports. Every download is handed to Android's Downloads, and a selection's summary no longer has a Saved line, since only the picker ever filled it.
- HushPinterest's short messages now show as Pinterest's own toasts. When a dialog is open, a message is long or has more than one line, or the Pinterest build's toast code isn't what the patch expects, they stay Android toasts.

## Behind the scenes

- The release receipt, the patch verifier and the device lease now hold the patched app to Android 10 (API 29), the same floor the settings patch sets since the Android 9 code went. They still expected API 28, so a target whose own floor was below 29 would have failed the receipt.
- While a release hold keeps the published index behind source, the release check now wants the bug report form to name the published release with the Pinterest build it was made for. It used to pair the published version with source's newer build, a combination nobody filing a report would have.
- The privacy doc now follows Pinterest's launch event, which carries the full URL the app was opened with, to both of its uploads: `v3/callback/event/` and `v3/callback/track_funnel/{event}/`. Disable analytics already stops both.
- The privacy doc now lists every header Pinterest puts on its API requests, with where each value comes from and whether a patch covers it. The advertising ID header is the only one a patch changes today.
- The header table now explains the last two. `X-Pinterest-AppState` only says whether the app is in front and online. `X-Pinterest-Platform-BID` is Pinterest's `_b` browser cookie, which the app keeps in Google Block Store (backed up to the cloud when Block Store offers end-to-end encryption), so it can survive a reinstall or a move to a new phone.
- The privacy doc now follows the install ID to all of its uses. Besides its own header it's Pinterest's signed-out ID, AppsFlyer's `unauth_id`, and the ID on analytics, push and reCAPTCHA events. A signed-in emulator kept its session, feed and search after the ID was swapped for a fresh one, so no hook is planned for it.
- System share sheet now checks, when you patch, that Pinterest gives a pin the share kind the patch makes pin links for. A build that numbers its kinds differently is refused instead of sharing a board's id as a pin link. The fixture tests cover that refusal and the two ways the sendable's constructor can stop naming its id and kind.
- Long-press download now checks that a menu button's detach handler really cancels the spring driver the patch clears, by finding the cancel call on that driver, not just a call that reads it. The fixture tests pin 14.39.0's spring fields and refuse a handler without the cancel.
- The patch verifier's System share and long-press checks now match the patch. The sendable's id and kind have to be its own fields written through itself, the springs reset needs a zero that isn't the button's register, and the spring driver has to be one the detach handler cancels.
- `scripts/test-app-inventory.ps1` checks the inventory tool on two tiny real APKs in `scripts/checks/inventory-fixture`, every section and the diff between them, in PowerShell 7 and 5.1. The script contract suite runs it, and `scripts/checks/build-inventory-fixtures.ps1` rebuilds the APKs from their Java sources.
- The Pinterest reference docs now describe 14.39.0. The APK facts, class and method names, endpoints and resource names were checked against the 14.39.0 build, with the old 14.38.0 name kept next to each one that moved. The patch reference covers all 27 patches. The signed-in screen survey and the runtime measurements are still the 14.38.0 runs, and the docs say so.
- The patch reference records the push sign-up check from a fresh emulator install. Without Fix push notifications, Firebase refused the sign-up with a 403. With it, the same install registered with Firebase.
- A fixture run that passes every check is now kept under a key made from the bundle, the APK, the patch selection and the hash of every verifier script, and a later run with the same key reuses it instead of patching Pinterest again. The release push gate patches each declared fixture once and the release receipt reads those runs. `scripts/patch-for-device.ps1` can sign the gate's patched APK for a phone when its key matches. A changed input means a full run, and a failed run is never kept.
- The push gate now runs the unit tests and lint in a quick Gradle pass before the fixture suite, so a broken test stops the push in minutes instead of after the Pinterest APK runs. Each pass waits for its own slot in the build queue.
- The script contract tests now parse every tracked PowerShell file, so a syntax slip in a script that only runs on a release or with a phone shows up on the next script push.
- Releases now run in stages from `scripts/release/release.ps1`: prepare, preflight, gate, build and publish. Each stage checks that the one before it finished, and running one again after it's done changes nothing. The CHANGELOG cut refuses any bullet that isn't a one-line Pinterest or Tooling entry and names it. The GitHub notes carry every bullet of the section. `publish-release.ps1` pushes the index commit as soon as the release is up and ends with `verify-published-index.ps1`. The notes and index text come from `release_text.py`, which has its own unit tests. (#3)
- `scripts/app-inventory.ps1` lists what a Pinterest build talks to and what it reads about the device. That covers its Retrofit endpoints with their verbs, the startup tasks, the hosts its code names, who opens connections, the SDK packages, and who reads the advertising ID, Android ID, install referrer or device identifiers. The lines come out sorted, with renamed packages written as `~`, so `-BaseApk` can diff two builds. The [privacy notes](docs/pinterest-14.39.0-privacy.md) now carry the 14.39.0 inventory and what changed from 14.38.0.

## Reported issues

Where each report on the tracker stands with this release.

- #6, ads getting through (@darenrue). Hide ads now checks inside the rows of pins on Home and under a pin you open, where an ad could slip past before. The store cards with a shop name and a tag icon, like the Target one in the report, aren't paid ads, so Hide ads leaves them. `Hide shopping and product pins` now hides them, and it starts off, so turn it on under Feed. The issue stays open until it's confirmed on your phone.
- #5, save downloads to a folder you choose (@boox3). New here. `Pick a download folder` under Pin actions saves pins straight into any folder in Pictures, DCIM, Download or Documents. `Save in Pinterest's folder` puts them in Pictures/100PINT/Pins with Pinterest's own saves.
- #4, one patch source for every Hush app (@Stark-0505). Still open. HushPinterest is still its own source in this release.
- #3, matching the Morphe template's release setup (@Stark-0505). Partly in. The patch index now goes up in the same step as the release, so Morphe Manager offers the update as soon as it's out, and a check after every release confirms the index matches. Moving to the template's own release workflow is still open.
- #2, Download pin said Pinterest had no original image (@Stark-0505). Fixed in 0.0.5. Download pin gets the original image behind the size Pinterest shows.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushPinterest as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushPinterest
3. Download Pinterest **14.39.0**, version code **14398020**, as the universal APK, and patch it. It needs Android 10 or newer.
4. Uninstall the stock Pinterest first, since Android won't put one over the other. Save anything you keep only on the phone before you do. Your boards and pins come back when you sign in.
5. Sign in with your email and a Pinterest password. If you joined through Google or Facebook, tap **Forgot your password?** on Pinterest's login page to set one first.
6. Right after your first patch, export Morphe Manager's signing key (Settings, then System, then Import & export, then Signing key) and keep it somewhere private. Updates only install over a Pinterest signed with that same key.

Already on HushPinterest? Skip steps 4 and 5. Patch 14.39.0 with the same key and install it over the one you have.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Pinterest APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#install). `SHA256SUMS.txt` is signed with the HushPinterest release key, fingerprint `FCE5 ECE3 182A 647B 3AF2  C5ED 2DC3 5E8D 5C00 E8A6`. [How to check a download](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#verify-a-release-download).

## Naolib vélo 3.6.1

### ✨ Fonctionnalités

- Affichage de la carte avec Morphe microG, avec un lien de téléchargement si le composant nécessaire est absent.
- Fenêtre au premier appui sur un parking : nom, état, places disponibles, capacité et heure de réception des données, lorsque ces informations sont fournies par Naolib. Le bouton « Voir le parking » ouvre ses détails.
- Parkings favoris enregistrés sur le téléphone : ajout, suppression et liste classée par nom. La sélection d’un favori recentre la carte sur le parking et affiche sa fenêtre.
- Mémorisation de la dernière position de la carte, du zoom, de l’orientation et de l’inclinaison.
- Suppression des contrôles locaux de proximité pour ouvrir les véloparcs (500 m) et déverrouiller les vélos (100 m). Un compte, la localisation et un accès valide au service restent nécessaires.
- Présélection des quatre patchs Naolib dans Morphe.

### 🐛 Corrections

- Maintien des parkings déjà chargés lorsque leur actualisation renvoie une liste vide, grâce au patch « Conserver les parkings ».
- Correction du démarrage de l’application modifiée et du plantage introduit par l’intégration de la carte.
- Interception de l’ouverture directe des détails d’un parking pour afficher d’abord sa fenêtre d’information.
- Utilisation des dernières données reçues pour les favoris ; la disponibilité est indiquée comme non actualisée lorsqu’aucune donnée récente n’est chargée.

### 📝 Textes et nettoyage

- Noms et descriptions des patchs Naolib, Keepcool et Leboncoin en français.
- Suppression des anciens patchs expérimentaux liés à la signature et à la carte.
- Documentation d’installation et d’utilisation de Naolib mise à jour.

Le patch de carte nécessite [Morphe microG](https://morphe.software/microg) avec son moteur de carte ; la version 7.2.1 est compatible. Les services Google Play doivent rester installés. Le chargement d’une nouvelle zone de carte dépend toujours du réseau et du moteur de carte.

This release gathers everything since v0.9.0 and brings 87 patches for Facebook 582.0.0.50.54, up from 86. The new one is `Unlock app icons`, which lets you pick any icon on Facebook's App icon page. New switches add a Watch history shortcut, keep a reel's time above its progress bar, stop link history in Facebook's browser and hold back camera roll processing. Saves whose only sound is xHE-AAC now get sound most players can play, and the Reported issues list below maps each report this release touches.

New in this release

- New patch, `Unlock app icons`, under Appearance (issue #109). Facebook already carries every icon on its App icon page and keeps most of them for Facebook Plus. With the switch on you can pick any of them, and Facebook switches your home screen icon to it and keeps it when it restarts or you update Hushfacebook. Facebook puts its own icon back on the first start after an update, and the switch stops that. Turned off, your pick stays until the next update, so pick the blue icon first if you want it back sooner. It's in Manager's default selection with its switch off.

- `Stop link history in Facebook's browser`, a new switch under Privacy that comes with Open links in external browser and starts on. Links that still open in Facebook's own browser, like Facebook's pages or any link on a phone with no other browser, aren't recorded for your link history or sent to Facebook as pages you visited. The browser just never builds its two link recorders, which is what it does when Facebook turns the feature off. Login, checkout and autofill keep working, and your Enhanced browsing setting stays as it is.

- `Hold back camera roll processing`, a second switch in Hold back analytics uploads under Privacy, which starts off. The processing behind camera roll sharing suggestions goes through your photos and videos, runs Facebook's models on them and uploads photos with what it found, and another job tells Facebook how many photos and videos you have. Facebook's server decides whether they run, and the app asks one check before it schedules or runs the work. With the switch on that answer is no, so Facebook cancels the work it scheduled, and the count job is cancelled too. Photos you pick to post go another way and never ask it.

- `Show a reel's time`, a new switch right below Keep the progress bar that starts on (issue #73). While the bar is kept, a reel's elapsed and total time stay above it and keep counting. Turn it off to see the time only while you drag, as before.

- `Watch history shortcut`, a new switch under Menu that starts off (issue #114). Turn it on and holding Facebook's icon offers Watch history, the videos and reels you've watched, when there's room next to Facebook's own shortcuts. The Menu's Settings and privacy group gets a Watch history row too. Both open Facebook's Videos you've watched page.

Fixes

- Open and Share on a finished save only answer their own buttons now. Another app on the phone could send Facebook the same request with a guessed file address and get it to open or share a video or photo Facebook had saved, with no tap from you.

- When a piece of Hushfacebook fails to load, Facebook keeps running. An error like that at app start or while opening a screen used to close Facebook every time, and pausing Hushfacebook didn't help.

- The `Share sheet items to hide` list closes with the settings page when you rotate the phone or Facebook closes the screen. It used to stay up over a window that was already gone, and it now follows the page's colors too.

- On a Facebook build that reads the loop setting in a way the reel hook can't use, the play reels once switch is refused while patching. Before, that build's reel player would fail to load.

- `Share sheet items to hide` calls Facebook's Muse item Muse. It showed up as "Share to hatch", Facebook's name for it inside the app.

- A reel's link from Copy link loses the `s=yWDuG2&fs=e` Facebook 582 adds to every copied reel, as long as Sanitize sharing links is on. Those two only say the link was copied.

- `Open on a chosen tab` set to Feeds opens the Feeds page again on Facebook 582 when your tab bar has no Feeds tab. The page showed for a moment and then Facebook jumped back to Home, because 582 treats its own Feeds links as links to Home. It now opens the page the way the Menu's Feeds row does.

- With `Material You theme` in dark mode, the comments under a post take your palette on Facebook 582. Each comment row draws its own gray box there, which the theme didn't reach, so the list stayed Facebook's gray while the rest of the sheet changed (issue #37).

- With `Material You theme` in dark mode, the box under a link post's picture, where the site name and title sit, takes your palette too. On some accounts Facebook sends that box a gray of its own, which the theme didn't reach, so it stayed gray in the middle of an otherwise themed post (issue #37).

- `Accent color` reaches the blues Facebook's server picks for a screen. A profile's Add to story, Message and Sign up buttons, links in a profile's bio and Marketplace's For you tab and location name now take your color in light and dark mode. They stayed Facebook's blue before, while the tab bar and the chips around them changed. Facebook blue and Pause leave them as Facebook draws them.

- In light mode, `Accent color` now tints the pale blue behind a selected chip, like Marketplace's For you pill. That fill stayed Facebook's light blue while the text on it changed, so a teal label sat on a blue pill. It's now a light shade of your color at the same brightness, and the label stays at least as readable as Facebook's own.

- After you update Hushfacebook, the settings page no longer shows a line like "Hushfacebook 0.7.1 targets Facebook 581" left over from the last release check. That line came from a check made before the update and named the older release's Facebook build. It now waits for the next check.

- The `Mark as seen button` eye sits in a story's top row now, next to the arrow and the three dots, instead of floating over the picture (issue #117). It also hides while you swipe to the next person's stories or drag a story down to close it, and comes back once the story stops moving. Before, it stayed put at the top of the screen through both.

- `Keep the progress bar` works on every reel now (issue #73). Short reels, which Facebook gives no bar at all, get one too, and their caption moves up to leave room for it like a longer reel's does, so the bar no longer sits on the caption. The bar also moves smoothly. Facebook only moved it about ten times a second, so it crept along in little jumps.

- `Open the Messenger app` finds a Messenger installed under another package name, like a copy made with Clone app, and the Get Messenger card stays hidden for it (issue #116). The top bar's Messenger icon used to look only for Meta's own package, so with a renamed copy it fell through to Facebook's Chats.

- Saved reels whose only sound is xHE-AAC play with sound in more players now (issue #14). Some gallery apps played them silent. Hushfacebook turns that sound into AAC-LC while it saves, also with Save videos other apps can open off, as long as your phone has an AAC encoder, and the picture keeps its full quality.

- The Lock Facebook cover tells a screen reader that Facebook is locked, marks its heading, and reads the reason line out when it changes.

Other changes

- The README tells people who patched in Manager's Expert mode before how to pick up the patches that are new to the default selection, since Manager keeps an Expert selection as it was.

- Clearer wording in a few places. The Tab to open on summary names the switch you'd actually turn off (Hide the Friends tab) instead of the patch name. The save toast for a video WhatsApp may refuse says to open Downloads in Hushfacebook settings to fix it. One save toast got its missing period, and the Pause list spells "recolored" like the rest of the app.

- The `Messenger` and `Instagram` rows under Links say what to pick on newer Android, where that app's Open by default page offers `In the app` and `In your browser` instead of an `Open supported links` switch. Picking `In your browser` for the official Messenger frees facebook.com and www.facebook.com, so they stay selected for Hushfacebook (issue #111).

- Block ad telemetry also stops several of the ways Facebook sends your phone's advertising ID. The job that posts it with your limit-tracking choice is stopped, and so are the launch event that carries it next to your device id, the GraphQL report of it and the install event sent from the first login screen. Other apps on your phone that ask Facebook for the ID get the empty answer Facebook gives when Google Play services has none, and Facebook no longer logs which app asked. The code that registers ad views and clicks with Android's own ad measurement returns right away, and so do the check of that measurement's status and the test ad audience job. A Facebook build that moved one of these still gets the rest, and the patch log says which one kept running.

Reported issues

- #109 Unlock the paid Facebook icons: the new `Unlock app icons` patch under Appearance lets you pick any icon on Facebook's App icon page.

- #114 Shortcuts for Reels and Watch history: the new `Watch history shortcut` switch under Menu adds a Watch history shortcut to Facebook's icon and a Watch history row to the Menu.

- #73 Keep the reel progress bar visible: `Keep the progress bar` covers short reels too and moves smoothly, and the new `Show a reel's time` switch keeps the elapsed and total time above it.

- #117 Mark as seen button glitch: the eye sits in the story's top row and hides while a story is moving.

- #37 Material You in dark mode: the comments under a post and the box under a link post's picture take your palette.

- #14 Saved videos playing silent in some gallery apps: saves whose only sound is xHE-AAC get AAC-LC sound, with the picture at full quality.

- #116 Opens Chats instead of Messenger: the Messenger icon now finds a Messenger installed under another package name, like a Clone app copy.

- #111 Links from Messenger opening in Messenger's browser: the Messenger and Instagram rows under Links say what to pick on newer Android so facebook.com links stay with Hushfacebook.

- Already in Hushfacebook and seen working since the last release: #84 `Hide the tab bar while scrolling` (AMOLED too), #65 the Material You colors on the tab bar, #98 `Share the post's own link`, #104 `Hide group buttons in the share sheet` and #107 `Hide the Follow link on posts`.

Behind the scenes

- A release's notes can map the reported issues it touches. Bullets under a `### Reported issues` heading in the CHANGELOG show up in their own Reported issues block, after the changes.

- The release's index step now moves the Facebook build in the repository description along with the version and patch count. After the 582 port it had left the description on 581, and the release facts check refused the index push until it was set by hand.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 1.34.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfacebook source.
2. Patch Facebook `582.0.0.50.54`. On most phones that's build `475417104`, the arm64-v8a one. Phones with a 32-bit processor take build `475417036`, the armeabi-v7a one.
3. Install over your current patched Facebook with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Facebook APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook#install).

Look over a diagnostic report before you share it. The filter can still miss private text it doesn't recognize.

What was checked

Local checks passed: 2418 runtime tests and 870 patch tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. All 87 patches applied without forcing to Facebook 582.0.0.50.54, both the arm64-v8a and the 32-bit build, and the only manifest changes are the four permission renames that let it install beside Meta's apps. I also patched 582 with every patch on an arm64 Samsung phone and on an emulator. Facebook opened signed in with no crash on both. On the phone the tab bar slid away while scrolling with the AMOLED theme, the Material You tab accent showed on the selected tab, Copy link gave a post's own link and the Follow link stayed off posts. On the emulator Play reels once stopped a reel on its last frame, the share sheet lost its group buttons, the Watch history shortcut opened Facebook's page and a save of a reel with only xHE-AAC sound played in Google Photos with sound.

HushThreads v0.0.13 has 19 patches for Threads 450.0.0.51.78 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so you need Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer.

Two patches are new, Hide the Instagram button and Hide ghost post bubbles. Morphe Manager's default selection now holds every patch but three, and Threads' push process no longer piles up threads when you come back to the app.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#7](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/7) asked to hide the Instagram button on profiles. The new `Hide the Instagram button` patch takes it off your profile and everyone else's. Its switch is in HushThreads settings under More settings > Appearance, and it starts off.
- [Hushfeed #122](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushFeed/issues/122) asked about the thought bubbles on Threads profile pictures. The new `Hide ghost post bubbles` patch takes them off. Its switch is on the same Appearance page and starts off too.
- [#6](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/6) found thousands of threads in Threads' push process. 0.0.12 fixed the main cause. This release also closes the push process every time Android stops its service, so the next start is a fresh one, and the process closes itself if it ever runs past 600 threads. Both fixes come with every build. I tried it on my phone by coming back to Threads six times, two minutes apart, and each time the push process started fresh and closed again. It's also the most likely cause of the battery drain someone mentioned on Reddit.
- [#5](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/5) asked for a pure black (AMOLED) theme. `Pure black dark mode` works on Threads 450 and is in Manager's default selection now, so you don't need Expert mode for it. Turn it on under More settings > Appearance.
- [#4](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/4) asked to keep your place when you come back to Threads. `Block background-return feed refresh` is in the default selection now as well (its switch is Keep feed position on return, under Feed), and the release check makes sure all four of its hooks land in Threads 450.

I'll keep each of these open until whoever reported it tells me it's working for them.

## Threads

- This release patches Threads 450.0.0.51.78 only, the newest stable version. 449.0.0.54.82 and 448.0.0.54.85 aren't offered any more, so if you're still on one of them, update Threads to 450 before you patch. From here on each release moves to the newest stable Threads and drops the one before.
- New `Hide the Instagram button` patch takes the Instagram button off the top of profiles, yours and other people's, and leaves the other buttons where they are. Its switch is on the Appearance page under More settings and starts off. Restart Threads after you change it.
- New `Hide ghost post bubbles` patch takes the little thought bubbles off profile pictures, the one on a profile and the row of them at the top of your feed. The pictures and the ghost posts themselves stay, and tapping a picture works as before. Its switch is next to Hide the Instagram button on the Appearance page and starts off. Restart Threads after you change it.
- `Hide suggested users` now keeps the Suggested for you accounts off profiles too, yours and other people's, and leaves the rest of the profile alone. It's the same switch under Feed, still on by default, and Search and Activity keep their suggestions. A profile that's already open keeps what it showed until Threads draws it again.
- `Disable video autoplay` now also holds an Instagram video shown inside a post, trend previews and the videos in ad cards, so they wait for a tap the way feed videos do. It's the same Tap to play videos switch under Feed, and the full-screen viewer still plays and pauses them as before. This passes fixture checks on Threads 450 but hasn't been tried on a device yet.
- The 0.0.12 fix for threads piling up in Threads' push process now comes with every build. It used to ride on `Restore screens on re-signed builds`, so a build made in Expert mode without that patch went without it. Without it, the push process on a re-signed build can stop and restart itself in a loop that piles up thousands of threads in under a minute. It's now part of `HushThreads settings`, which every other patch needs, and has no entry of its own in the patch list.
- Threads' push process still gained about seven threads every time you came back to Threads after more than a minute away. Android stops the push service when Threads has been in the background for about a minute but keeps its process, and each restart left the stopped service's threads running. Now the push process closes once its service has stopped, and the next start gets a fresh one, the same as after Android frees memory. It also keeps count of its own threads while it runs and closes itself past 600 (it normally runs about 60), so a runaway like the thousands in one report can't keep growing. Like the fix above, it comes with every build.
- Morphe Manager's default selection now holds every patch but three, so you don't need Expert mode to get `Disable video autoplay`, `Pure black dark mode`, `Max image quality`, `Disable screenshot detection` or `Block background-return feed refresh`. Those five start with their switches off, and a fresh patch looks like the Threads you know until you turn things on in HushThreads settings. `Change version code` stays out because it changes the version Android sees, so going back to stock Threads means uninstalling. `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates` stay out because they change Threads when you patch and there's no switch to undo them. Turn on Expert mode to pick those three.
- If you'd picked one of those five patches before and never changed its switch, the switch starts off after you update. HushThreads keeps no record of the build you came from, so it can't tell you meant it on. Look these over in HushThreads settings and turn back on the ones you want. Under Feed that's Keep feed position on return, Tap to play videos and Full size photos. Under Privacy it's Hide screenshots from Threads, and under Appearance, in More settings, it's Pure black dark mode. A switch you'd already turned off stays off.
- `Save photos and videos` moves from Feed to a Downloads group in Expert mode's patch list, the same name its page has in HushThreads settings.
- Every patch description says what the patch does, where its switch is in HushThreads settings and how that switch starts, so Manager's list tells you what you're getting before you patch.
- Patch descriptions in Morphe Manager are rewritten in plain English. Each one says what the patch changes, why you might want it, and ends with where its switch is and whether it starts on or off.
- Setting rows in HushThreads settings are reworded in plain English, with a restart reminder on Pure black dark mode. Translations for German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish are updated to match.
- A few messages are clearer about what happened and what to do next: a failed download, the cancel hint while saving, an unreadable reply from GitHub, and the status line on the overview. Translations are updated to match.
- The settings home page ends with Support HushThreads, which opens the Ko-fi page in your browser. If nothing on your phone can open it, a tip shows the address and Threads keeps running.

## Docs

- The README's Trust user-added certificates section now says which connections your certificates reach. Android's standard check honors the patched file, but Threads' own network stack still wants one of Meta's built-in keys on the connections it pins, so a debugging proxy can't read that traffic.
- Added a Threads APK reference and app audit covering feed ads, tracking identifiers, analytics patch boundaries, and customization opportunities. Added patch authoring guidance and corrected the install example to use the primary 450 target.
- Added a stock 450 walkthrough with settings screenshots, measured network and background observations, and explicit battery-measurement limits. Confirmed the profile Instagram button and separate profile suggestions, and expanded the patch guide's registration and coverage checks.

## Tooling

- Settings and Turkish translation tests now match the wording shipped in HushThreads.
- The desktop CLI runs, bundle merges and the resource, register, signing and fingerprint checks now wait for a slot of the machine's build queue when `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names one, and run straight away when it doesn't. Before, they started beside whatever builds were running and the queue never saw them.
- The device scripts no longer cut a longer device lease down to 20 minutes when they renew it, so a lease taken for a long check can't lapse in the middle of it and hand the device to someone else. They also read a lease's end time in UTC under PowerShell 7. A lease written with a `Z` used to read back as local time, which west of UTC kept an expired lease looking valid for hours.
- The patch tests that read the Threads fixtures run as their own Gradle task, `:patches:fixtureTest`, with each fixture's path and SHA-256 as its inputs. A change to the fixtures reruns only those tests, and a fixture swapped for another of the same size and date still counts as a change. Each build's dex is now read and parsed once per test run rather than on every lookup. `:patches:test` still runs every test, and refuses a run where a fixture test skipped with the fixture folder set.
- The pre-push gate runs Gradle twice. Everything but the fixture tests goes first, so a failing quick test or lint stops the push in minutes, and the full run with the fixture tests comes second. `scripts/release/release.ps1 -Stage preflight` runs the quick checks a release needs in about five minutes: the advisory comparator, the script contracts, that same quick patch run, the translation and release-check tests, both lints and the release facts.
- A release can patch each Threads fixture once instead of twice. `verify-all-patches.ps1 -KeepIn <folder>` keeps a passing run with a stamp naming the bundle, APK, patch list and CLI by SHA-256, and `build-release-receipt.ps1 -AppliedDir` reads a kept run whose stamp still matches and runs every check on it. Any other fixture is patched as before.
- The release check accepts `* **Docs:**` bullets in the section being released, the way it accepts `* **Tooling:**` ones. Morphe Manager shows neither, and neither counts as a Threads change. Before, a release whose section held a Docs bullet was refused.
- A release now runs in five stages from `scripts/release/release.ps1`, one command each, in the order `prepare`, `preflight`, `build`, `publish` and `index`. Prepare makes the version and changelog edits for you to review and commit. Preflight now runs the release text tests too, then pushes the prep commit through the gate. Build patches each fixture once for the receipt and tags the commit only after everything passed. Publish checks every hosted asset against the built one before it changes the repository description, and index writes the index commit and pushes it. A stage won't run before the one it follows, and one that stopped part way can be run again.
- Release preflight clears the test results its filtered extension run leaves behind. Gradle keeps only the classes a run touched, and the push right after read that partial set for the commit it carried and stopped there, so preflight's own push failed every time before the gate ran a test. Build still reruns every test before anything is counted.
- The register check accepts the version code `Change version code` writes. `verify-all-patches.ps1` applies every patch, that one included, and the check refused the build because its version code no longer matched stock. With the patch selected, the patched build now has to carry exactly the raised code, and without it the codes still have to match.
- The final APK check now holds `Block background-return feed refresh` to its own contract, the way it already holds `Hide ads` and five other patches. It finds Threads' four return checks in the stock build by what they log and how they decide, and the patched build has to ask the extension once at each: first thing in the hot-start decision, right before the reset to main feed returns, right before the warm-start check stores its answer, and where For you's swap joins its two answers. Left out, the patch has to leave those four methods as Threads wrote them. Before, a hook that still landed but no longer saw the answer it's there to change would've passed.
- The final APK check now holds `Disable video autoplay` to its own contract too. It finds PostVideo and its playback effect in the stock build by the notes Compose leaves in them and works out which of PostVideo's booleans decides whether its video plays (the fourth on 450). The patched build has to ask the extension about that flag right before every call a single post or a carousel makes to PostVideo, with any branch to the call landing on the question, and PostVideo and the effect have to stay as Threads wrote them, so the full-screen viewer plays as it always has. Left out, nothing may ask and those methods stay stock. Before, a build that dropped the hook or put it on the wrong flag passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- That `Disable video autoplay` contract now covers the calls an Instagram post, a trend preview and an ad card make to PostVideo as well. It reads which bit of PostVideo's default mask stands for the play flag. Where a call sets that bit (the trend preview and the ad card on 450), PostVideo ignores the flag it's handed, so the hook has to clear the bit and load the default into the flag before it asks, and nothing may read either register after the call. The full-screen viewer has to stay as Threads wrote it. The register check gains test builds that skip the Instagram post, ask without clearing the bit, load the wrong default, change the viewer or read the mask again after the call, and only this contract refuses each one.
- The final APK check now holds `Pure black dark mode` to its own contract as well. It finds Threads' theme in the stock build by the note Compose leaves in it, along with the helpers the theme builds its colors in (on 450 the #101010 gray is loaded in one of those, not in the theme), and it finds the dark and light color schemes the theme reads by their colors. Every #101010 load there has to hand the gray to the extension right after, on its own register, and each of the dark scheme's #101010 backgrounds (two on 450) has to ask right before the scheme is built. The light scheme keeps its own #101010 untouched, so light mode looks as it always has. Left out, nothing may ask and those methods stay stock. Before, a build that dropped a load hook or the dark scheme's background hooks passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now holds the HushThreads row in Threads' own settings to a contract too. It finds Threads' settings list, its settings row and the row it draws Accounts Center with in the stock build by the notes Compose leaves in them, and it reads which case of the list draws More settings from the entry names Threads keeps. The patched build has to ask the extension for the HushThreads row once, right where that case ends, on the composer the case draws with. The extension's row has to call Threads' Accounts Center row with its own title, subtitle, icon and click, and the click has to be a kind Threads' row can take. Every other patch depends on `HushThreads settings`, so the check expects the row in any build with a patch selected. Before, a build that dropped the row or drew it in the wrong place passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now proves the spare registers `Sanitize sharing links` borrows are really free. Each of its link hooks puts the post's code and its author's name in registers of its own, and the hooks in Copy link and the resumed shares load the post into one as well. The check walks the stock method from the spot each hook goes in, down every branch and into the catch blocks around it, and refuses a build whose hook writes a register Threads still reads there. Before, it only checked that those registers didn't clash with each other, so a hook that wiped out a value Threads still needed passed, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now makes sure `Restore screens on re-signed builds` only borrows registers that are really spare. The patch writes three registers at the top of Threads' signature wrapper before the stock code runs, and the check requires all three to be locals of that method, below the register `this` sits in. Before, a build whose wrapper had fewer registers than the patch assumes could have the patch overwrite `this`, and it passed because the check only compared the register numbers to the ones the patch expects. Only the fixture tests would've caught it.

## Update

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.13 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
